consequence.statement: The option is deprecated and has no effect; setting it does nothing.

original.statement: Helm value enableRuntimeDeviceDetection is deprecated and is a no-op in 1.16.

consequence.statement: Any value configured for the Helm option enableRuntimeDeviceDetection is ignored from 1.16.0 on, because the option is a no-op.
consequence.remediation: Remove enableRuntimeDeviceDetection from your Helm values. Check that the behaviour you get without it is acceptable.

corrected.statement: In Cilium 1.16.0 the Helm value enableRuntimeDeviceDetection is deprecated and is a no-op, so any value set for it is no longer honoured.

decision.reason: [ev-99f86df45975] says the Helm option `enableRuntimeDeviceDetection` "is now deprecated and is a no-op" in 1.16. A no-op means a configured value is no longer honoured starting with this release. That matches setting-ignored, not deprecation, which covers an option that still works and breaks only in a later release. The proposed statement itself says setting the option "does nothing", which contradicts the deprecation kind.
